findings.title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript allows XSS on the Discourse origin
findings.body: The embed layout renders `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` with the raw Referer header inserted into a JavaScript string literal without escape_javascript/html escaping. The `ensure_embeddable` before_filter only validates that the referer's *host* equals SiteSetting.embeddable_host, so an attacker making a direct HTTP request (where the Referer header is fully attacker-controlled, e.g. `http://<embeddable_host>/', alert(document.cookie), '`) can break out of the string literal and execute arbitrary script in a page served from the Discourse origin. This is a reflected XSS; the value must be escaped with `j()`/escape_javascript before interpolation.

findings.title: Imported RSS content is stored as raw HTML with skip_validations and rendered with `raw`, enabling stored XSS
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, which makes `Post#cook` return the raw content verbatim (no markdown/sanitization pipeline). The RSS path in `Jobs::PollFeed` passes `i.content` (fully controlled by whatever the feed at feed_polling_url contains) straight into import — unlike `import_remote`, which at least runs the content through ruby-readability's tag/attribute whitelist. `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. A compromised or malicious feed entry containing `<script>` or `onerror=` handlers is stored and executed on the Discourse forum and on every page that embeds the comments iframe. The feed content needs sanitization (e.g., Sanitize/Nokogiri whitelist) before being stored as raw HTML.

findings.title: URL interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute in the 'imported from' footer
findings.body: `contents << "...#{url}..."` interpolates the embed URL directly into HTML that is later stored via the raw_html cook method and rendered with `raw`. The `^https?://` regex check on line 11 does not exclude single quotes, `>` or other markup characters that can appear in a URL's path/query (e.g. `http://embeddable-host/?x='>`). This allows attribute breakout and markup injection into the stored post. The URL should be HTML-escaped (and the href properly quoted) before interpolation.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error; the embed view fails to render
findings.body: Line 6 closes the header if/else with `<%- end if %>`, which ERB compiles to the Ruby fragment `end if ` — a modifier `if` with no condition, a syntax error. Every render of the embed view (the success path when a topic exists) will raise ActionView::Template::Error / SyntaxError and return a 500 to the embedding site, making the whole feature non-functional in the topic-found case. It should be `<%- end %>`. The controller specs don't catch this because `TopicView` is stubbed with a mock, so the template never renders against a real topic view.

findings.title: Referer-based authorization is trivially spoofable, allowing unbounded job enqueueing and forced fetching
findings.body: Access control for /embed/best relies solely on the Referer header matching SiteSetting.embeddable_host. Any non-browser client can set an arbitrary Referer header, so anyone on the internet can hit the endpoint and cause `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` for arbitrary embed_url values. The TopicRetriever throttle is only 60 seconds per exact URL string, so an attacker can vary the URL (query strings, paths) to enqueue an unbounded number of jobs, each of which causes the Discourse server to make an HTTP request to the embeddable host (a limited but real SSRF/abuse vector) and, when feed polling is enabled, synchronously executes the entire Jobs::PollFeed run inside the job. Rate limiting at the controller level and/or a global cap on retrieve jobs is needed.

findings.title: Discussion replies rendered with `raw post.cooked` include any HTML users managed to post
findings.body: The embed view renders each post with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. While normal posts go through the cooking/sanitization pipeline, this view bypasses all of the markup filtering Discourse normally applies when displaying cooked content (e.g., the whitelist applied elsewhere), so any HTML that survives into `cooked` for any post in the topic — including raw_html posts created by other import paths or plugins — is executed verbatim in a frame that is served from the Discourse origin with `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. Combined with the raw_html import path this widens the XSS surface; cooked output should be passed through the same sanitization used by the main topic renderer.

findings.title: Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE can leave the throttle key without a TTL, permanently blocking retrieval
findings.body: `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)`. If the process dies (or the Redis connection drops) between the two calls, the key exists with no TTL and never expires, so that embed_url is throttled forever — the topic is never retrieved and the embed shows the loading page indefinitely. Use a single atomic command (e.g., `SET key 1 EX 60 NX` available via the redis gem, or a Lua script) so the expiry is always set.

findings.title: PostCreator jobs are enqueued inside the wrapping transaction, before the TopicEmbed row commits
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` wraps `creator.create` in `Topic.transaction` and only creates the `TopicEmbed` record *after* the post is created. PostCreator's `enqueue_jobs` (process_post, feature_topic_users) runs while still inside this outer transaction. If the subsequent `TopicEmbed.create!` fails — most plausibly in the race where two concurrent retrieve jobs for the same embed_url both pass the `where(embed_url: url).first` check and the second hits the unique index — the whole transaction rolls back, but the already-enqueued Sidekiq jobs referencing the rolled-back post/topic are not un-enqueued, and `TopicTrackingState.publish_new` messages have already been published on MessageBus for a topic that never committed. The unique-index race should also be handled (rescue RecordNotUnique / create the embed first or use find-or-create).

findings.title: Nil `i.content` (or a feed error) crashes the whole poll, and retry is disabled
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has `content`; RSS feeds that only provide `description` (or ATOM entries with only a summary) will raise NoMethodError on nil, aborting the entire `poll_feed` run partway through — items after the offending one are never imported. Since the job has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the failure is silent until the next hourly run, which will fail at the same item. `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is likewise unguarded, so a transient network error kills the run. Guard for missing content (fall back to `i.description`) and rescue per-item/feed-level errors.

findings.title: `feed_key` is dead code — the modified/ETag check it hints at was never implemented
findings.body: The `feed_key` method builds a Redis key (`feed-modified:<sha1 of feed url>`) but nothing in the class ever reads or writes it. Either the conditional-fetch logic was dropped accidentally, in which case the key is misleading dead code, or the intent was to skip polling when the feed is unchanged — either way it should be removed or wired up. As it stands every poll re-parses and re-imports the full feed each hour.

findings.title: `force: true` added to an already-shipped migration can silently drop the top_topics table
findings.body: This PR modifies the existing CreateTopTopics migration (2013-12-23) to add `force: true`, which makes `create_table` DROP the table if it exists. For any database that already ran this migration and then re-runs it (e.g., `rake db:migrate:redo`, or environments that replay migrations), all top_topics data would be destroyed. Editing historical migrations also means schema state diverges between deployments that ran the old version and the new one. The `force: true` should be reverted here (it belongs only in brand-new migrations, if anywhere).

findings.title: Origin check via `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` is a weak substring match
findings.body: The postMessage handler validates the sender with `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. it accepts any message whose origin string appears anywhere in the configured discourseUrl. Because it is a substring (not prefix/exact) match, an origin that happens to be contained in the URL string passes; e.g. a discourseUrl of `http://discourse.example.com` accepts an event from origin `http://d` (host `d`) or any origin that is a substring of the URL. The consequence is limited to setting the iframe height today, but the correct check is an exact/parsed comparison (e.g. compare `e.origin` against the URL's `protocol + '//' + host`), since future message types would inherit the flaw.
